findings.claim: The new collector always selects surrogate mode or collects all public read-write members contractlessly; it never checks T for [MessagePackObject]/[DataContract] or reads its [Key]/[IgnoreMember] annotations. Consequently, an attributed T does not have its declared keys and membership honoured, violating an explicit acceptance criterion.

receipt_plan.detail: Generate a formatter for a type carrying [MessagePackObject] with integer [Key] values and an [IgnoreMember] member, without setting SurrogateType. Serialize it and assert the generated formatter uses those integer keys and omits the ignored member; the current implementation instead emits contractless string-keyed public members.

findings.claim: An unrelated change replaces the fail-closed guard for hash-based collections of non-whitelisted key types with EqualityComparer<T>.Default. Untrusted MessagePack can therefore reach an arbitrary type's non-collision-resistant GetHashCode implementation, re-enabling hash-collision denial of service that this method explicitly exists to prevent.

receipt_plan.detail: Under MessagePackSecurity.UntrustedData, deserialize a hash-based collection whose key type is not whitelisted and assert TypeAccessException is thrown without invoking that type's GetHashCode. The changed fallback instead permits the default comparer and the test fails.

findings.claim: The pre-existing blanket rule that metadata-only types receive no formatter remains deliberate for ordinary discovery. The new feature is an explicit opt-in exception through GeneratedFormatterCollector rather than a reason to remove or flag TypeCollector's metadata early return.

receipt_plan.detail: [L11] records that referenced-assembly types deliberately receive no analysis or formatter through ordinary TypeCollector discovery; REQ-2129 separately requires the explicit [GeneratedMessagePackFormatter] opt-in path.

interpretations.label: A
interpretations.summary: Use contractless string keys by default and implement the optional SurrogateType design: the collector reads [Key]/[IgnoreMember] from the named surrogate and matches its members to T, as this change does.

interpretations.label: B
interpretations.summary: Use serialization attributes directly on T instead of adding a surrogate contract: when [DataContract]/[DataMember] are present, derive membership and keys from DataMember (Order/Name), keep contractless behaviour only when no contract attributes exist, and remove or bypass the SurrogateType collection branch.
